ambient_trade.text: Selling salt in {town}, 40 gold a sack. Fair price for a fair road. Anyone buying in bulk?
Buying wool in {town} at {gold} gold a bale. Good wool, honest weight, no tricks :)
Caravan leaving {town} tomorrow with spare cart space. Half the escort cost for anyone who shares it.
Anyone want iron from {town}? I'll take {gold} gold for the lot, not a copper less.
Salt is up to {gold} gold in {town}. Hold your stock a week, the margin is worth the wait.

encounter_trade_offer.text: I'll pay {gold} gold for safe passage and not a copper more, {player}. Think it over, the road is not getting cheaper.
{gold} gold for the lot, {player}, delivered in {town}. That is a fair price and you know it.
For you, {player}, {gold} gold and I'll throw in a sack of salt. Deal, or do you want to haggle?

encounter_greeting.text: Ser {player}, I have no wish to fight. My wagons carry salt, not grudges. Name your price and we can all go home.
Ser {player}, {persona} of {my_faction} here. Are you carrying anything worth trading, or just passing through?
Good to see you, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction} here. Fancy a quick trade before the next toll gate?

player_raided_my_village.text: Burning {village} was a poor investment, {player}. Now every merchant will charge me more for escorts.
{player}, you burned {village}. I won't pretend that doesn't hurt. Name a figure for the damages and we can talk.
{player}, the ashes at {village} cost me a lot of business. I'd rather settle this in coin than in steel.
Raids on {village} push every price up, {player}. Pay the damages and the road stays open for both of us.

war_declared.text: {my_faction} is at war with {enemy_faction}. Every war is a tax on the roads, and I'm the one paying it.
War between {my_faction} and {enemy_faction}. Wonderful. Grain doubles in price and the bandits get bolder.
Word is {my_faction} has declared on {enemy_faction}. My wagons are keeping off the eastern roads until it settles.

peace_made.text: Peace between {my_faction} and {faction} at last. Good news for the roads, and my prices are already dropping.
{my_faction} and {faction} have made peace. I'm sending a caravan through before the tolls go up again.
Peace with {faction} means lower insurance on my wagons. Finally some sense from the lords.

released_by_player.text: {player} released me without ransom. Could have asked for a fortune. Not sure what to make of that, honestly.
You released me instead of asking for ransom, {player}. I won't forget that, nor the price of my pride.
Thank you for releasing me, {player}. I owe you a discount on salt, and I always pay what I owe :)
{player}, you let me go rather than hold me for ransom. Let's talk prices next time we cross paths.

beat_by_player.text: {player} beat my {troop_count} men in the field. Lost wagons, lost men, and I still have to sell the salt.
{player} beat my {troop_count} troops fair and square. Bad for my purse, good for my respect.
{player}, that field cost me {troop_count} troops and two wagons. Good fighting, but I still expect a fair price.
Ser {player}, you took {troop_count} of my men today. I won't forget it, but I'll still talk prices with you.
Well fought, {player}. Losing {troop_count} men hurts, but I respect a good opponent. Let's talk prices after.

whisper_beg_help.text: {player}, {enemy_faction} is pressing {fief} hard. Help me hold it and I'll pay you well, with a standing trade deal.
{player}, I'm losing {fief} to {enemy_faction}. Send your men if you can. Name your price and I'll meet it.
The walls of {fief} won't hold against {enemy_faction} for long. Help me, {player}, and I'll make it worth your while.
Old friend {player}, {fief} will fall to {enemy_faction} soon. I know it's a big ask, but I'll pay in salt.

ambient_complaint.text: Lost another wagon to {faction} longbowmen on the way out of {town}. Bad for business, I tell you.
Bandit toll on the road again. Whoever is thieving out there, my wagons are not your fundraiser.
{rival} thinks tolls are a fine way to pay for roads. Some of us actually have to carry the cost.
Every road tax in {town} takes a bite out of the margin. I count my coins twice before I load a wagon now.
Eleven wagons gone to the longbows and I still sell them salt. Business is business, but it hurts.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain on the road to {village} again, so the mud is worth a fortune to the cart makers.
Anyone else notice salt prices climb every time it rains in {town}? Makes me think the weather is a trader too.
Lag on the eastern route cost me half a morning. Still, the wagons don't mind a slow road.
Heard {village} has a good harvest this season. Might be worth a detour for a cheap cart of grain.
A quiet week on the roads is good for my wagons and worse for my purse, to be honest :)
